A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TaxBuilder, RealMix and PC2 framework, renamed from Feedbacker to SCAN. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original judge-accuracy experiments, evaluations of 17 LLMs, human query-quality assessments and contamination analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original judge evaluations on SCAN-HPD, RewardBench-v2 and RMB, evaluations of 21 LLMs, and retained human query-quality and contamination results.

M1.justification: TaxBuilder, RealMix and PC2's auxiliary-response comparison, weighted criteria and baseline-guided scoring remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and corresponding appendix prompts match. Expanded explanations of baseline guidance and existing analysis tools do not establish new method components.

E1.justification: v3 adds RewardBench-v2 and RMB's helpfulness subset, including best-of-N response selection and RewardBench-v2's factuality, instruction-following, math, safety and focus cases (Appendix B.1–B.2). This substantially expands evaluation coverage beyond the retained six-domain, 3,343-query dataset and 636-example human-preference dataset, which are renamed.

E2.justification: The quantitative pairwise and baseline-assisted naive pointwise comparators in v1 Table 2 disappear from v3 Table 2, as does the separate win-rate comparison in v1 Table 3. NCD survives as direct metric decomposition, alongside renamed pre-comparison variants. Appendix D retains illustrative pairwise examples, not the removed quantitative comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 changes the default judge from QwQ-32B to DeepSeek-R1; v3 Table 2 also tests three other judges. The profiled-model roster expands from 17 to 21, with new best-of-N and auxiliary-model control experiments. Both appendices specify 1–3 scoring; v1's conflicting main-text 1–5 instruction disappears, so a clean actual scale switch is not established.

E4.justification: v3 replaces point-scale and criteria-count ablations with auxiliary-model composition, number and ordering studies (Tables 5–7). The earlier sample-size stability, token-cost and limited-data win-rate analyses are removed. GPT-OSS coding and knowledge diagnostics replace the GPT-4o/XML walkthrough, and Appendix C.3 adds concrete examples for the existing analysis tools.

E5.justification: v1's rank-stability and winner-agreement experiments report 20 resamplings and variability summaries (Sections 5.1–5.2, Figure 6 and Table 3); these disappear in v3. New accuracy tables provide no corresponding repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. The retained child-node ranking standard deviations describe capability variation rather than repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the 0.8318 PC2 accuracy using QwQ-32B with 0.6962 using DeepSeek-R1 and adds other judge results; these are not same-setting performance changes. v3 adds external-benchmark results and a revised 21-model leaderboard led by GPT-OSS-120B at 242.24. Among retained models, Gemma-3-27B overtakes QwQ-32B overall. Earlier domain-specific judge accuracies and XML findings disappear.

T1.justification: The insertion formalism, criteria-weight construction, scoring formulation and Algorithm 1 retain their mathematical substance. Condensing the standard pairwise description and simplifying naive-pointwise notation do not introduce substantive mathematical reasoning changes. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds PC2's higher-than-pairwise accuracy and reliability with limited data as a principal contribution. v3 drops those explicit assertions, instead claiming gains over classic judging methods and centering its contributions on capability characterization. This changes the scope of the evaluator claim beyond the framework's renaming.

C2.justification: The XML-specific optimization hypothesis is replaced by interpretations of GPT-OSS specialization, model selection and uneven training-knowledge coverage. New ablation interpretations attribute improvements to diversity and declines with additional models to redundancy or noise. Limitations expand beyond multimodality and safety to explicitly include honesty, factuality, hallucination and fairness.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 substantially expands operational documentation for existing tools, specifying a ranking-gap threshold of 5, top/bottom 20% variability thresholds and the QwQ-32B summarizer. v3 also discloses baseline-answer generation parameters, fallback decoding settings and annotator payments. These additions improve reproducibility without establishing changes to the underlying tool procedures.

R1.justification: v3 adds a benchmark-feature comparison table and references for the new benchmarks, models and expanded multimodal/safety limitations, while removing some evaluation references such as HD-Eval. The substantive comparisons with coarse taxonomies and EvalTree in Appendix A.1 remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, experimental narrative and conclusion are substantially rewritten around SCAN and capability understanding. The challenge–solution introduction is replaced, Section 5 is rebuilt, Appendix B.2 is introduced, and future directions and limitations move into the main text.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Table 2 changes from domain-wise columns to judge-specific blocks; new benchmark and ablation tables appear. Earlier diagnostic plots are replaced by a programming-language bar chart and knowledge treemaps. Most taxonomy and prompt figures are retained but resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens external validation through additional benchmarks and judges, and makes the analysis tools substantially easier to reproduce. However, it removes direct pairwise comparisons and repeated-sampling reliability evidence while retaining Section 3's assertion that 19 samples per tag ensure statistical representativeness. These gains coexist with reduced support for an important retained claim, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
